unruled:gate:asset.claims_bonus#1.class: no gate defect; 60%, QPP and specified-plant cases are refused before the gate, WIDE accepted
unruled:gate:asset.claims_bonus#1.reason: asset.claims_bonus is computed (placed in 2025 and asset.bonus_choice ≠ none), not asked as worded in the helper label. Aircraft, long-production property and QPP are refused by asset.kind_excluded and asset.long_production; fruit and nut plants are farming property outside the class table (asset.outside). Reuse and recycling property is refused by the screen, so the extra question is an accepted WIDE.

findings.evidence: i4562 p. 6, "Property with a long production period and certain aircraft ... special depreciation allowance of 60%". Out of scope: an aircraft is refused by asset.kind_excluded (tick 'A building, land, a vehicle, an aircraft, a film or a recording') and property with a long production period or qualified production property by asset.long_production (tick 'Built to order over a long period, or “qualified production property”'); both feed asset.screen, so asset.screened refuses through asset.cost. Also, asset.claims_bonus is not a yes/no the filer answers: it is asset.bonus_choice ≠ 'none' (choices 'Yes: the special depreciation allowance', 'The 40% allowance...', 'No: I elect not to take any special allowance'), so a filer taking 60% would not pick 'none'.

i4562 pp. 7-8, QPP "by designating up to 100% of the depreciable basis". QPP is named in the asset.long_production tick ("Built to order over a long period, or “qualified production property”"), and QPP is nonresidential real property, which asset.kind_excluded ("A building, land, ...") also refuses; either Yes refuses through asset.screened. A 2025 QPP never reaches asset.used_before_if_bonus.

i4562 p. 6: the specified-plant allowance "applies only for the tax year in which the plant is planted or grafted". Growing fruit or nut plants is farming, and a return with farm income or loss is refused by scope.farm ("In 2025, did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) have income or a loss from farming?"); the asset entries belong to Schedule C. The form also takes only property with a year placed in service (asset.placed), and the farming class is outside (class_lives.yaml c01_1: outside).

i4562 p. 7, reuse and recycling property "original use ... must begin with you". Such property is refused anyway (asset.screen item "qualified reuse and recycling property", through asset.industry_item_if_industry); asking asset.used_before costs one question.

unruled:gate:asset.industry#1.class: defect (low): the industry tick asks about the business, so item-defined reuse/recycling property owned outside a recycling business skips the refusal; energy property covered by the class question
unruled:gate:asset.industry#1.reason: Energy property is caught by asset.class (Table B-2 D, E and F, mapped to outside). Reuse and recycling property is defined by the equipment's exclusive use (i4562 p. 6), and a business that is not a recycler truthfully leaves the tick "Used in a utility, energy, recycling, rent-to-own, racetrack or loan-financed dealer business" blank, so asset.industry_item (and its refusal) is never asked; the tool then computes plain MACRS where an elected-out class would owe the 50% section 168(m) allowance. Gathering and transmission lines owned outside a utility are recorded under the same bug as open residuals. Floor-plan lessors: wording only.

findings.evidence: i4562 p. 10, 5-year property includes "Certain energy property specified in section 168(e)(3)(B)(vi)". findings.evidence: i8962 p. 5: employer-sponsored coverage includes a group plan bought through one's own business; f8962.other_coverage's help says 'If you are not sure, answer Yes; the next questions settle it', and f8962.job_offer and mec_job_enrolled count any job's plan. Low.
f8962.job_offer's help: 'Do not count COBRA or a retiree plan that was not taken, or the months of a waiting period'. A Yes here is settled there. Safe.

unruled:gate:s3.adoption_any#1.class: no gate defect; two medium wording residuals on 'adopt' read by the date the child came home, as ruled before
unruled:gate:s3.adoption_any#1.reason: A child placed before 2024 whose adoption became final in 2025 is an adoption 'since the start of 2024' by the decree, but the question and help do not say so; the residual stands under BUG-0620 (9). The wide finding costs one question.

findings.evidence: i8839 p. 1, case 2 (special needs, final in 2025, credit even with no expenses) and case 3a (foreign child, final in 2025). The question "Since the start of 2024, did you ... adopt a child, or pay (or have an employer pay) costs toward adopting one?" is Yes by the decree date, but a family that counts adoption from placement answers No, and s3.adoption ("Did the adoption become final in 2025") is not asked; the credit of line 6c is then lost rather than refused. Medium; remedy a help sentence ('count an adoption in the year a court made it final, even if the child came home earlier'). As ruled before on the false-no review of this gate.

i8839 p. 3, Foreign Adoption, employer payments before the final year are excluded in the final year. As the finding before: the same reading of 'adopt' also skips scope.adoption_benefits, which is gated by s3.adoption_any. Medium.

i8839 p. 3, Domestic Adoption. A 2024 adoption paid for and final in 2024 answers Yes and is asked s3.adoption and s3.adoption_earlier, both truthfully No; nothing is refused (fixture redesign.credits.adoption_2024_complete). One extra question.

unruled:gate:s3.adoption_asked_if_any#1.class: no gate defect; 2024 payments and employer payments are asked by sibling questions under the same outer gate
unruled:gate:s3.adoption_asked_if_any#1.reason: s3.adoption covers only 2025 events by design; 2024 payments for a U.S. child are asked by s3.adoption_earlier and s3.adoption_us, employer payments by scope.adoption_benefits, and a 2024 carryforward by s3.prior_forms, all under s3.adoption_any.

findings.evidence: i8839 p. 1, case 1a. s3.adoption_earlier_if_any and s3.adoption_us_if_earlier are gated by s3.adoption_any, not by s3.adoption; a Yes to both refuses s3.line7 with s3.adoption false (fixture redesign.credits.refuse.adoption_earlier_us: s3.adoption false, adoption_earlier and adoption_us true, line 7 refused at s3.adoption_us_if_earlier).

i8839 p. 1, the four cases. Case 1a by s3.adoption_us; cases 1b, 2 and 3 by s3.adoption (final in 2025 or paid in 2025); employer benefits by scope.adoption_benefits ("Did an employer pay or repay any of the adoption costs ... code T", gated by s3.adoption_any, a Yes ends the interview); case 4, a carryforward, by s3.prior_forms (2024 Form 8839). The inner question is one branch of a tree that covers the cited text.

i8839 p. 1, case 3b, employer-provided benefits in 2025. scope.adoption_benefits asks whether an employer paid or repaid any adoption costs and refuses the return, so the employee's own No at s3.adoption loses nothing.

unruled:gate:s3.adoption_final_if_adopti.class: no gate defect; a not-final adoption gives no 2025 credit that the stepchild question could change; one low residual
unruled:gate:s3.adoption_final_if_adopti.reason: The stepchild line is read only by s3.adoption_if_any, which also requires a final adoption, so its default false on a not-final adoption changes no value; 2024 payments are refused through s3.adoption_us; employer benefits through scope.adoption_benefits.

findings.evidence: i8839 p. 2, a spouse's child's expenses are not qualified; p. 3, a U.S. child's 2025 expenses on a not-final adoption are credited the year after payment. s3.adoption_stepchild_if_final is read only by s3.adoption_if_any, which requires s3.adoption_final_if_adoption true; with a not-final adoption no refusal and no credit arise (fixture b1mutB.s3.adoption_not_final: s3.adoption_if_any false, line 7 $0), so 'treated as qualified' changes nothing.

i8839 p. 3, Domestic Adoption, 2024 payments credited in 2025. Asked by s3.adoption_earlier and s3.adoption_us under s3.adoption_any; a Yes refuses s3.line7 (fixture redesign.credits.refuse.adoption_earlier_us).
i8839 p. 3, employer payments excluded in the year of payment. scope.adoption_benefits (gated by s3.adoption_any) asks whether an employer paid or repaid any adoption costs and refuses the return.

i8839 p. 3, Line 1. The form's source asks "Did that adoption (or, if more than one, any of them) become final", but the interview asks "Was that adoption final by the end of 2025?"; a filer with one final and one pending adoption may answer for the pending one, No, and the final adoption's credit is not refused. Rare; low. Remedy: carry 'or any of them' into the question.

unruled:gate:s3.prior_other_forms#1.class: no gate defect; the design's accepted residuals; one wide
unruled:gate:s3.prior_other_forms#1.reason: A carryforward with no 2024 return is the design's BUG-0620 (8); Form 8582-CR beside 'a four-digit number' is BUG-0620 (4); a Yes for an unrelated form costs two questions.

findings.evidence: f8859 p. 1, Line 4; f8396 p. 2. A credit carried from 2023 or earlier by a filer with no 2024 return: the help says "If you did not file for 2024, answer No". The design's named residual BUG-0620 (8). Low.
The question's "a page headed 'Form' and a four-digit number" beside Form 8582-CR (a suffix). The follow-up s3.prior_forms names 8582-CR. Low; BUG-0620 (4).
A 2024 return with only Form 8962 or another unrelated form answers Yes and is asked s3.prior_amt and s3.prior_forms, both No; nothing is refused.

unruled:person.mw_business#1.reason: Wording of the business test; both routes give the same tax on these excludable payments.

findings.evidence: The question restates i1040gi p. 24's test ('If you are a sole proprietor in a business of providing home care services') as 'Do you run a business of your own that provides home care?'; scope.medicaid_waiver covers care of someone living in your home, whose payments are excludable either way, so the route chosen changes where they appear, not the tax.
A family caregiver who reads the parenthetical as describing their 1099-NEC pay answers Yes and is refused; extra refusal only.

unruled:gate:person.eligible_educator#1.class: no gate defect; the calendar-year reading of '900 hours' is a low wording residual
unruled:gate:person.eligible_educator#1.reason: The question restates the instructions' test, but its 'In 2025' opening and missing help let a filer count only 2025 hours for a school year that straddles the year end. Filed as one low wording entry.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 93, 'who worked in a school for at least 900 hours during a school year'. The interview asks 'In 2025, did you work in a school ... for at least 900 hours during a school year?' with no help, so a teacher who left in June 2025 (or started in August 2025) can count only the calendar-2025 hours and answer No; person.educator_expenses_if_educator is then zero (up to $300 lost).
As finding 0, for a teacher who started in the 2025-26 school year: the question does not say that the school year, not calendar 2025, measures the 900 hours.

unruled:gate:person.has_hsa#1.reason: The HSA listing question asks about any HSA held in 2025; the gate's citation is now Part VII (BUG-0865 fixed).

findings.evidence: (same claim as an earlier subject, rechecked) $f8889: 'Answer Yes even if nothing went in or out in 2025' (questions.yaml:4628), so an idle HSA with an old excess is listed and person.x_hsa_prior_excess ('Before 2025, was more put into your HSA than the limit ...') is asked and refuses.

The gate now cites f5329 p. 2, Part VII, 'or you had an amount on line 49 of your 2024 Form 5329' (person.yaml:7732; BUG-0865, fixed by BUG-1381). Line 49 is 6% of the smaller of line 48 or the HSA value on December 31, 2025, so a nonzero amount needs an HSA existing in 2025, which the listing question counts.

unruled:gate:person.ira_files_8606#1.class: no gate defect; prior-year basis with a 2025 distribution or conversion is refused on the Form 1099-R
unruled:gate:person.ira_files_8606#1.reason: The three NARROW cases all have a 2025 traditional IRA Form 1099-R, where retirement.ira_basis refuses a filer with earlier nondeductible contributions; the SOURCE finding is the same split of the Who Must File conditions between the two places.

findings.evidence: Each traditional IRA Form 1099-R (distribution or conversion) asks retirement.ira_basis, 'Have you ever put money into a traditional IRA that you did not deduct on a tax return?' (help: 'If any of your earlier tax returns includes Form 8606, answer Yes. ... a Yes ends the interview here'), which refuses through retirement.special. The gate person.ira_files_8606 opens line 2 only for a 2025 nondeductible contribution; basis from earlier years with a 2025 distribution or conversion is refused on the 1099-R. f8606 Part I, 'You took distributions from a traditional IRA in 2025 and you made nondeductible contributions ... in 2025 or an earlier year'.

Each traditional IRA Form 1099-R (distribution or conversion) asks retirement.ira_basis, 'Have you ever put money into a traditional IRA that you did not deduct on a tax return?' (help: 'If any of your earlier tax returns includes Form 8606, answer Yes. ... a Yes ends the interview here'), which refuses through retirement.special. The gate person.ira_files_8606 opens line 2 only for a 2025 nondeductible contribution; basis from earlier years with a 2025 distribution or conversion is refused on the 1099-R. A partial Roth conversion is a 1099-R distribution from the traditional IRA, so the same question is asked.

Each traditional IRA Form 1099-R (distribution or conversion) asks retirement.ira_basis, 'Have you ever put money into a traditional IRA that you did not deduct on a tax return?' (help: 'If any of your earlier tax returns includes Form 8606, answer Yes. ... a Yes ends the interview here'), which refuses through retirement.special. The gate person.ira_files_8606 opens line 2 only for a 2025 nondeductible contribution; basis from earlier years with a 2025 distribution or conversion is refused on the 1099-R. The repaid distribution is itself a 2025 Form 1099-R from a traditional IRA with basis; the basis question is asked on it. A qualified reservist repayment is refused through scope.reservist_repaid (ira.reservist_repaid).

The gate covers the 2025-contribution bullet of i8606 Who Must File; the bullets for distributions or conversions with earlier basis are handled by retirement.ira_basis on each 1099-R, as above. The line's citation names only the first bullet; no case drops.

findings.evidence: Payments not on a Form 1099 are person.mw_other: on line 1d only if chosen as earned income and then excluded on Schedule 1 line 8s (person.line8s), otherwise out of income; the scope.medicaid_waiver payments are for care in the filer's home and excludable, so the Schedule C route would give the same tax.

unruled:gate:person.sav_trad_if_ira_owne.class: no gate defect; a contribution not yet made is not entered, and SEP/SIMPLE cases are WIDE
unruled:gate:person.sav_trad_if_ira_owne.reason: The interview counts 'Money put in by April 15, 2026 for 2025' and person.ira_owner counts 'one opened in early 2026 for 2025'; a filer who has not yet contributed enters the contribution when it is made.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 98, line 11, 'made, or that will be made by the due date'. person.ira_owner asks whether the person has an IRA 'now', with help 'one opened in early 2026 for 2025' counts, and person.sav_trad says 'Money put in by April 15, 2026 for 2025 counts'. A filer who has not opened or funded the IRA when filling in the return is outside what the questions can record; opening and funding it before filing answers both Yes. Not a gate defect.
SEP or SIMPLE money or a withdrawn contribution: the help says 'Do not count money that went into a SEP IRA or a SIMPLE IRA'; a Yes only leads to the amount question. Safe.

unruled:gate:person.simple_open_year#1.class: no gate defect; the 1963 to 1965 band is set by birth year, and the open years are the January 1 births
unruled:gate:person.simple_open_year#1.reason: person.simple_age puts anyone born 1963 to 1965 in the 60 to 63 band without a question; 1962 and 1966 are asked because a January 1 birth in those years attains 64 or 60 on December 31, 2025.

findings.evidence: person.simple_age: born from age.cut_64 (1962) up to the year before age.cut_60 (1966) goes to person.simple_age_60_63_years, which returns person.catchup_age60_63 whenever person.simple_open_year is false. Born 1963, 1964 or 1965 is in the 60 to 63 band ($5,250); the gate's otherwise value is read only for 1962 and 1966.

p560 p. 16, 'in a tax year in which they attain age 60, 61, 62, or 63'. Under the day-before rule the project applies (person.born_jan1's help), a person born January 1, 1962 attains 64 on December 31, 2025, and one born January 1, 1966 attains 60 that day; so the birth date does decide the band in those two years, as the gate says.
Everyone born in 1962 or 1966 is asked so that the January 1 births can be told apart; one question, no amount dropped.

unruled:gate:person.under16_open_year#1.class: no gate defect; a filer born 2011 or later is under 16 by birth year and refused
unruled:gate:person.under16_open_year#1.reason: person.under16 is true for anyone born after 2010 without a question; only 2010, where a January 1 birth is 16 on December 31, 2025, is asked. The age-16 refusal is the owner's entry check (amb.2025.filer_under_16).

findings.evidence: person.under16 is 'birth_year > age.cut_16 (2010)' or (born 2010 and person.under16_at_year_end_if_open_year). A filer born in 2011 or later is under 16 from the first branch and is refused (household.filer_under16); the open-year gate exists only for 2010.

amb.2025.filer_under_16: the text has no minimum filing age; the owner chose to refuse a filer or joint spouse under 16 at the end of 2025 as an entry check citing the Self-Select PIN sentence, without claiming the text forbids the return. The citation is the one sentence that names age 16, as recorded.

The refusal deliberately ignores first-time-filer status and the signing method (amb.2025.filer_under_16, owner's decision 2026-10-22); a filer born in 2010 who is under 16 is refused. Over-refusal by design.

unruled:gate:person.x_edu_account#1.reason: The gate's citation is shared with other Form 5329 lines; the gate leans to yes by design.

findings.evidence: f5329 p. 3, Part IX is part of a shared locator also cited for Part II; the gate (any 529, Coverdell or ABLE account) and its gated questions (excess contributions, taxable distributions) follow Parts II to VIII. Citation only.
f5329 p. 1, Part II: 'Complete this part if you included an amount in income'. Asking every account holder two questions costs only questions.

unruled:gate:person.x_edu_account#1.adjudication: round F sampled-review adjudication, 2026-11-21 (Claude agents, RUBRIC2)

unruled:gate:dependent.other_only_spouse.class: no gate defect; a false gate sends the spouse's competing claim to the general tie-breaker refusal
unruled:gate:dependent.other_only_spouse.reason: The gate is household.mfs (f1040.status = mfs). When it is false, or when the answer is No, dependent.spouse_settles is false and dependent.tiebreak_unsettled takes dependent.tiebreak_spouse_or_other, then dependent.tiebreak_other, which refuses whenever dependent.other_claimant is Yes and the other person is a taxpayer or the child is also the filer's qualifying child. The spouse's claim is never treated as zero: it is refused. Only the case the tool computes (spouse the only other person, not claiming, filer a parent: p501 p. 17 Example 6; amb.2025.mfs_spouse_qc) depends on the gate.

findings.evidence: p501 p. 15 tie-breaker. Executed (fixture mfsl4.other_relative_too, married filing separately, other_claimant Yes, other_only_spouse No): other_only_spouse_if_mfs false, spouse_settles false, tiebreak_other true, and f1040.line19, dependent[kid].ctc_amount and line 27a refuse at dependent[kid].qc_tiebreak / eic_tiebreak ('The tie-breaker rules are outside this tool'). A third person who is also a claimant therefore gives a refusal, not a dropped spouse claim.

i1040gi p. 17, '(other than your spouse if filing jointly)'. On a head of household return the gate is false and the path is the same as finding 0: dependent.other_claimant (help: 'On a separate return, your husband or wife counts') Yes leads to dependent.qc_tiebreak, which refuses (executed path as finding 0). No computed claim drops the spouse.

i1040gi p. 17. The gated question asks facts ('Is your husband or wife the only relative, besides you, who lived with this child for more than half of 2025 and could claim them?'). A No (an unsure filer, or a third relative) refuses at qc_tiebreak (executed, finding 0). A Yes missing a third non-parent relative leads to the spouse question; with the filer a parent claiming the child, the parent wins against a non-parent (i1040gi p. 21, 'If only one of the persons is the child's parent'), so the result is unchanged.

unruled:gate:dependent.ptc_files#1.class: defect: the question states only the single under-65 non-blind limits
unruled:gate:dependent.ptc_files#1.reason: dependent.ptc_files decides whether the dependent's modified AGI enters f8962 line 2b (dependent.ptc_magi_counted). A married dependent is refused before this matters (dependent.married, 'A married dependent is outside this tool'), and Form 8814 is refused (f1040.line16 on scope.f8814). The combined test is in the help. The 65-or-older or blind dependent has no stated limit: BUG-0861.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 10, Chart B, married dependents ($5 rule). A dependent who has ever been married is asked dependent.married ('Was this person married at the end of 2025, or is this person on a joint tax return...? A Yes ends the interview here'), which refuses at dependent.married_screen_qc / married_if_ever_married_qr ('A married dependent is outside this tool'). The $5 rule never reaches a computed return.

i1040gi p. 10, Chart B combined test. The help shown with the question states it: 'A dependent with both kinds must also file when the two together are more than the larger of $1,350 and their pay (up to $15,300) plus $450.'

i8962 p. 8, Form 8814 amounts. Form 8814 is refused: scope.f8814 ('This is the choice made on Form 8814. A Yes ends the interview here') feeds the refusal on f1040.line16 (scope.other_line16, 'Forms 8814, 4972, 8615...'). No computed return has a Form 8814 child.

i1040gi p. 10, Chart B: 'Your unearned income was over $3,350' for a dependent 65 or older or blind. The help says 'These limits are for a single dependent under 65 who is not blind' and gives no other limit; a filer applying the stated $1,350 answers Yes and the modified AGI is counted on line 2b though the dependent need not file (PTC understated). Not a refusal.

unruled:gate:household.married#1.class: no gate defect; one low wording residual on common-law marriage
unruled:gate:household.married#1.reason: The gate household.married is household.marriage_possible (status mfj, mfs or qss, or household.ever_married for single and head of household) and then household.married_dec31. The interlocutory decree is stated in the help. The common-law marriage is stated in the gate's help (household.ever_married: 'Count a marriage that has ended, and a common-law marriage') but not in married_dec31's help: BUG-0863. The WIDE is accepted.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 14 / p501 p. 6, interlocutory decree. household.married_dec31 help: 'A divorce that was not yet final on December 31 means you were still married'.

p501 p. 6, Considered married 2 (common-law marriage). The gate question household.ever_married says 'Count ... a common-law marriage', so the possibility is reached; the gated question 'Were you married on December 31, 2025?' and its help do not repeat it (the line source does, from BUG-0280). A filer who answers the two inconsistently skips household.considered_unmarried and keeps head of household.

p501 p. 6. Joint filers and legally separated filers who reach the question answer it; a Yes asks the considered-unmarried question, which costs a question only (household.filing_status_conflict and hoh tests read it). No amount dropped.

unruled:gate:household.mfs#1.class: no gate defect; the head of household lived-apart test is a separate question
unruled:gate:household.mfs#1.reason: household.mfs_living_if_mfs feeds only married-filing-separately tests: household.mfs_apart_all_year (ssb worksheet line 8, line 6d, ira, s1, person) and household.mfs_apart_last6 (eic.mfs_same_home, f2441 line A). The head of household test for a married filer who lived apart is household.considered_unmarried ('You lived apart from your husband or wife for the last six months of 2025, you paid more than half the cost of your home, ...'), gated by household.married, not by this gate, and filing status is an input, so there is no circularity.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 15, Married persons who live apart. The head of household test reads household.considered_unmarried_if_married (asked of anyone married on December 31), not household.mfs_living. Every consumer of household.mfs_living_if_mfs is an MFS-only rule (grep forms/2025: ssb.yaml, eic.yaml eic.mfs_same_home, f2441.yaml line A, ira.yaml, s1.yaml, person.yaml), where together_late is the right default off MFS.

i1040gi p. 31, Line 6d. Every MFS filer is asked when they lived with the spouse; it also feeds eic.mfs_same_home and f2441 line A, so it is not idle without benefits. One question, no amount dropped.

unruled:gate:f1040.digital_assets#1.reason: The gate omits 'award' from its wording, which does not change an amount because prizes and awards are asked on their own; the sale case only over-asks.

findings.evidence: The gate reads 'get crypto ... as pay, a reward or new coins' while Form 1040 says 'reward, award, or payment'; a crypto prize can draw a No on the Digital Assets box. The amount is still reached: s1 asks 'Did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) have gambling winnings, or receive a prize or an award, in 2025?' independently of the digital asset gate, and the 8v question covers staking, mining, forks and airdrops, which the help names. The wording of the printed box is the only thing at stake.
A sale answers Yes by design ('sell, trade, spend or give any away'), as i1040gi p. 16 requires, and the gated line stays zero; this costs one question.

unruled:gate:f1040.estimated_any#1.class: defect: amended-return overpayment and joint payments sent by a former spouse are outside the gate wording (BUG-0897)
unruled:gate:f1040.estimated_any#1.reason: i1040gi p. 39 includes an overpayment applied from an amended return and joint payments with a former spouse; the gate names only payments sent and a 2024 refund applied.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 39, 'Include any overpayment that you applied to your 2025 estimated tax from your 2024 return or an amended return.' f1040.estimated_any names only 'a 2024 refund applied to your 2025 tax'.

i1040gi p. 39, 'If you got divorced in 2025 and you made joint estimated tax payments with your former spouse'. The gate's spouse clause is 'on a joint return' and the help says payments 'you send yourself'.
Form 1040 line 26 says 'amount applied from 2024 return'; the gate calls it 'a 2024 refund applied', which a filer who received no check may not recognize. Low part of BUG-0897.

unruled:gate:rec.has_mortgage_if_path#1.class: no gate defect; a form pointer and the spouse reading
unruled:gate:rec.has_mortgage_if_path#1.reason: rec.has_mortgage asks 'a refund or credit of home mortgage interest you deducted for 2024 (box 4 of Form 1098)'.

findings.evidence: p525 p. 24, 'the amount should be shown in box 4 of Form 1098'. The parenthetical is a pointer to where the amount usually appears; the question's test is 'a refund or credit of home mortgage interest you deducted'. Low.

unruled:gate:rec.has_other_if_path#1.class: no gate defect; earlier years and sales tax are refused, reimbursements are named
unruled:gate:rec.has_other_if_path#1.reason: rec.has_other asks 'a refund or reimbursement of something else you deducted on your 2024 Schedule A ... such as a casualty loss reimbursed'.

findings.evidence: p525 p. 27, separate worksheet per year. rec.not_2024 ('Was any of the money paid back in 2025 for something paid or deducted before 2024?', help 'For example a 2023 casualty loss reimbursed in 2025. A Yes ends the interview here') is asked after any Yes to scope.recovery (rec.not_2024_if_any), whatever the 2024 itemizing answer, and refuses.

p525 p. 27 footnote 2, sales tax refunds. rec.sales_tax ('Was any of the money paid back a refund of sales tax?', 'A Yes ends the interview here') is asked after any Yes to scope.recovery and refuses; p525 p. 27 footnote 2 is therefore never computed.
The question says 'a refund or reimbursement', with 'a casualty loss reimbursed' as its example.

unruled:gate:rec.has_property_tax_if_pat.class: no gate defect; the question asks about tax deducted for 2024
unruled:gate:rec.has_property_tax_if_pat.reason: rec.has_property_tax asks 'a refund of state or local real estate tax or personal property tax you deducted for 2024'.

findings.evidence: p525 p. 26, Worksheet 2a line 4 (taxes paid in 2024). The question's test is tax 'you deducted for 2024', which is tax paid in 2024 whatever period the bill covered; a bill paid before 2024 is refused by rec.not_2024.

unruled:s1.nol_before_limit_date#1.reason: Finding 0 covered: s1.nol_limit (forms/2025/s1.yaml; refusal on f1040.line15, 'Form 172, NOL deduction limitation (the 80% limit)') refuses whenever the carried loss is more than four times taxable income after deducting it, i.e. whenever the 80% cap could bind. Finding 1 covered by the amount question's help.

findings.evidence: i172 p. 1, NOL deduction limitation, '(b) 80% of the excess (if any) of taxable income computed without regard to deductions for NOLs, or QBI'. s1.nol_limit_test is s1.nol_amount_if_nol > 4 x (f1040.line11b - f1040.line14); f1040.line15 refuses on s1.nol_limit ('the limit of 80% of taxable income figured without the deduction may apply'). A post-2017-only filer above the cap is refused, not over-deducted.

i172 p. 1, Step 5. s1.nol_amount asks 'How much of that loss is still unused and carried into 2025?' with help 'Give what is still unused, after what earlier returns used'; that unused carryover is the deduction when the cap does not bind, and s1.nol_limit refuses when it may.

unruled:gate:s1.has_gambling#1.reason: The winnings question the filer sees is gross gambling winnings before losses, not the line 8b trade-or-business amount; a professional with no winnings has no Schedule C amount.

findings.evidence: The gate is computed from s1.gambling_winnings, whose filer prompt is 'How much did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) win from gambling in 2025, before subtracting any losses?' with no trade-or-business exclusion, so a professional's winnings make the gate true and s1.gambling_pro is asked.

p525 p. 33: 'professional gambling losses and expenses are limited to the amount of your winnings. This also means that a professional gambler cannot claim a loss on Schedule C (Form 1040) in a loss year.' With no winnings the Schedule C is zero, so skipping the refusal leaves every amount right.

The same p525 p. 33 limit ('professional gambling losses and expenses are limited to the amount of your winnings') makes positive winnings the only case where trade-or-business status changes an amount, so gating on winnings above $0 loses nothing.
A casual winner is asked the professional question and answers No; p525 p. 33, 'If you're in the trade or business of gambling, use Schedule C', gives them no Schedule C amount. Extra asking only.

unruled:gate:f8853c.has_periodic#1.reason: Line 20 zero implies line 26 zero in the terminal-only case; one WIDE.

findings.evidence: i8853 p. 9, Multiple Payees: "If you checked 'Yes' on lines 15 and 16 and the only payments you received were accelerated death benefits that were paid because the insured was terminally ill, skip lines 17 through 25 and enter -0- on line 26." With line 20 zero the tool also gives line 26 = 0, so suppressing line 15 loses no amount.
Line 20 above zero with no costs, reimbursements or other payee still asks the gated questions, whose answers are zero or No; extra asking only (rule 2).

unruled:gate:f8853c.periodic#1.reason: Fixed-amount wording follows i8853; variable periodic accelerated death benefits cannot be settled from the archived text.

findings.evidence: i8853 p. 8 defines "Per diem payments are payments of a fixed amount made on a periodic basis without regard to actual expenses incurred", while the line 19 caption (f8853 p. 2) and the filing chart (p. 9) say "per diem or other periodic basis" for accelerated death benefits without defining "other periodic". The question asks for "a set amount per day, week, month or other period, whatever the care cost" and f8853c.line19 "at a set rate". It would settle with IRS guidance (Pub. 502 or the section 7702B regulations) on whether variable periodic accelerated death benefits paid regardless of expenses are within line 19; not in the archived sources. Cost: such benefits are left off Section C.

Terminal-only per-diem accelerated death benefits answer Yes; the line 19 prompt then leaves out amounts "after a doctor certified that the person was expected to die within 24 months" (questions.yaml:4367-4368), so no amount results; extra asking only (rule 2).

unruled:gate:f8889.ask_former_spouse_fam.reason: Filers not uniform or not eligible every month take the month path, where months_family names the spouse's plan; an ineligible then-spouse only refuses.

findings.evidence: A changed-coverage filer answers the month questions; f8889.months_family asks month by month whether 'your spouse' had a plan covering more than one person, with help 'Your spouse's plan counts for a month in which the three conditions held for your spouse as well' (i8889 p. 4, rule 1), as ruled on the earlier subject.

Self-only all year but not eligible every month gives f8889.coverage_self = cov_changed, so the same month questions are asked and f8889.months_family counts the then-spouse's family months (i8889 p. 4, How To Complete Part I).
i8889 p. 4, 'both eligible individuals'; a then-spouse not eligible still draws a Yes and the refusal at f8889.line13_figured. Extra refusing only.

unruled:gate:f8889.inherited_any#1.reason: The account beneficiary's own final return is asked at f8889.owner_died; the earlier-year non-spouse case costs a question.

findings.evidence: i8889 p. 3, 'If the account beneficiary's estate is the beneficiary, the value of the HSA as of the date of death is included on the account beneficiary's final income tax return'. f8889.owner_died asks whether the person this Form 8889 is for died in 2025, and its wording includes an HSA whose beneficiary is the estate; it refuses. f8889.inherited_any is about someone else's HSA.
A non-spouse beneficiary of an earlier-year death answers Yes and picks 'Someone else, earlier year' in f8889.inherited_case, which refuses nothing. An extra question.

unruled:gate:f8889.mfs_ask#1.class: defect (wording) recorded for the present tense; the rest covered or presentation
unruled:gate:f8889.mfs_ask#1.reason: Joint returns split the family limit through the allocation lines; the present-tense spouse-HSA question is the false-no lane's BUG-0874.

findings.evidence: i8889 p. 7, Line 6. On a joint return the separate-HSA split is figured by the allocation lines (f8889.allocation, f8889.line6_split, person.hsa_share); the separate-return question is needed only because the spouse's side is not on this return.

The prompt 'Does your husband or wife have a health savings account' is present tense while the line (and i8889 p. 7, 'Spouses who have separate HSAs and had family coverage ... at any time during 2025') concern 2025; a spouse's HSA closed after taking 2025 contributions is answered No. BUG-0874, low.
The f8889 collection frame 'For this person (you, or your spouse on a joint return)' precedes a question asked only on a separate return; 'your husband or wife' still names the person. Wording only.

unruled:gate:f8889.testing_failed_figure.reason: A 2025 transfer refuses at f8889.ira_transfer; the filer-facing questions carry no timing ambiguity; the wrong disability No and the WIDE cases refuse, safe.

findings.evidence: A qualified HSA funding distribution made in 2025 is refused at f8889.line13_figured / line13_none through f8889.ira_transfer ('Was any money moved into your HSA straight from an IRA in 2025?'), so its testing period is never figured.

The filer sees f8889.ira_gap ('From the month of that transfer until 12 months after it, was there a month in which you could not have an HSA?'), not the helper's label; the months asked include 2025.

i8889 p. 2, 'other than because of death or becoming disabled'. A filer who reads 'stop being able to have an HSA' as closing the account answers No to f8889.disabled and is refused at f8889.testing_failed. Safe.

i8889 p. 8, testing period through the 12th month. f8889.ira_gap asks only the months of the testing period, so a loss of eligibility after it ends does not refuse through the transfer; any refusal through the last-month rule is safe.
i8889 p. 2: death also excuses the failure; the refusal is wider. Safe; the return of a person who died is rare here.

unruled:gate:retirement.cost_any_if_plan.reason: The death benefit exclusion is asked on the code 4 path; a survivor is not limited to own contributions.

findings.evidence: A beneficiary's payment (code 4) reaches retirement.death_exclusion, which refuses, as ruled on the earlier subject.
The question 'Was any of the money paid into this pension or annuity already taxed when it went in' is not limited to the filer's own payments, and the help says 'If you are not sure, answer Yes'.
Extra Simplified Method questions change nothing; safe.

unruled:gate:retirement.disability_if_pl.reason: Per-entry question; the spouse's 1099-R is asked about the spouse.

findings.evidence: retirement is a per-entry list: the Form 1099-R list is asked per person ('For this person (you, or your spouse on a joint return) ...'), and the per-person frame shows the spouse's entry 'About your spouse', so 'you' in a question about that entry is the person it was issued to (interview/README.md, the per-person frame; RUBRIC2 rule 4).

unruled:gate:retirement.is_code7#1.reason: Codes 1 and S at 59½ or older are now handled by exception 12 from the birth year; the code 7 gate is for the reverse case.

findings.evidence: retirement.miscoded (BUG-1193) applies exception 12 to a code 1 or S distribution of a person born in 1964 or earlier, and asks retirement.after59 for one born in 1965 or 1966; code J is refused (retirement.bad_code).

The code 7 gate looks for a code that does not fit (code 7 under 59½ refuses at retirement.code_screen); its citation is the generic line 2 sentence. No amount depends on it, as ruled on the earlier subject.
A code 7 distribution received after 59½ is asked the age question; one extra question.

unruled:gate:retirement.is_trad#1.reason: The IRA box on the form decides the kind; SEP, SIMPLE and inherited IRAs are traditional_ira.

findings.evidence: retirement.account: 'traditional_ira (the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box on Form 1099-R is checked; includes SEP and traditional SIMPLE IRAs), roth_ira (...), or plan (a pension, annuity, 401(k), 403(b) or governmental 457(b) plan)'; the IRA box is checked for an inherited IRA, an individual retirement annuity and a deemed IRA. The basis question's text names 'basis that came with an IRA ... from someone who died'.

retirement.account: 'traditional_ira (the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box on Form 1099-R is checked; includes SEP and traditional SIMPLE IRAs), roth_ira (...), or plan (a pension, annuity, 401(k), 403(b) or governmental 457(b) plan)'; the IRA box is checked for an inherited IRA, an individual retirement annuity and a deemed IRA.
A filer without basis answers No; one extra question.

unruled:gate:retirement.plan_death#1.reason: Combined codes are refused as another code; the rest costs coverage only.

findings.evidence: i1099r p. 15, 'enter Codes 4 and G'. retirement.code offers 'Any other code, two codes together (such as 7D or 4G)', which retirement.bad_code refuses.

The tool follows box 7 as printed; a payer's coding error is the payer's to correct. A Form RRB-1099-R has no code and is the 'other' answer, refused by retirement.bad_code. Cost: a mis-coded survivor payment is computed as a normal distribution.
Extra questions only.

unruled:gate:retirement.put_back#1.reason: retirement.rollover_any names conversions and does not say 'another' account; the WIDE finding costs questions.

findings.evidence: The filer sees retirement.rollover_any, 'Did any of this money go into a retirement account again (a rollover or a conversion), even if it was paid to you first?', with help 'Money moved into a Roth IRA counts'; a conversion is Yes and retirement.roth_moved refuses it (i1040gi p. 27, Exception 2).
The same question says 'a retirement account again', not 'another'; a redeposit into the same IRA is Yes (i1040gi p. 30, Rollovers).
An ordinary rollover is asked the four refusal questions; extra questions only.

unruled:gate:retirement.under59_if_code7.reason: A section 457 distribution coded 1 takes its exception in retirement.exception.

findings.evidence: A code 1 distribution goes to retirement.exception, whose list (e01 to e23) includes the section 457 exception; the code 7 gate concerns only a code 7 under 59½, as ruled on the earlier subject.

unruled:gate:sli.any_if_not_mfs#1.reason: Interest paid by others is now named in the gate's help; the WIDE case costs only questions.

unruled:gate:ssb.prior_year_pay#1.reason: A missed Yes only skips an election this tool refuses; the return without the election is a correct return. The WIDE finding costs a question.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 31, Line 6c: the lump-sum election is optional ('you may be able to reduce'). A Yes here leads only to ssb.lump_elect, whose Yes refuses; an RRB-1099 recipient who answers No gets a correct return without the election.
With nothing taxable the election question is still asked; one extra question.

unruled:s1.nol_ebl#1.reason: The 80% limit is refused by a computed gate at Form 1040 line 15; it is not this screen's job.

findings.evidence: s1.nol_limit refuses at f1040 line 15 ('Form 172, NOL deduction limitation (the 80% limit)') whenever the carried loss is more than four times taxable income after deducting it, which is conservative against i172 p. 2, 'the lesser of ... 80% of the excess (if any) of taxable income computed without regard to deductions for NOLs, or Qualified Business Income (QBI)'. Whenever the limit binds, the return is refused rather than computed with the full NOL.

unruled:gate:s1.nol_joint#1.reason: Only farming losses can be carried back, and a carryback is claimed on the earlier year's return; neither reaches this return unrefused.

findings.evidence: i172 p. 2: 'If you have an NOL for a tax year ending after 2020, only the farming loss portion, if any, can be carried back.' Farming is refused by scope.farm, and a carryback is claimed on the carryback year's return (i172 p. 3, 'Attach a Form 172 for each NOL to your Form 1040-X'), not as a deduction on line 8a of this 2025 return.

Spouses married in every year answer No to s1.nol_not_married and the NOL is computed; i172 p. 3, 'If you and your spouse were not married to each other in all years involved ... only the spouse who had the loss can take the NOL deduction.' Extra asking only.

unruled:rental.not_for_profit#2.reason: rental.not_for_profit: low-rent and relative cases are personal-use days; the profit test is the IRS wording.

findings.evidence: i1040se p. 5: personal use includes "Anyone who pays less than a fair rental price"; such days are asked at rental.personal_any. A profit-seeking landlord who ticks Yes because of the example is refused, costing coverage only.

A relative renting below a fair price makes every such day a personal-use day (rental.personal_any: "anyone stay[ing] free, below a fair rent"), so the unit is used as a home and is excluded (rental.excluded) or refused (rental.ws51) under p527 p. 28; a relative at a fair rent is an ordinary rental. A No therefore reaches the dwelling-unit rules that govern it.

p527 p. 24: "If you don't rent your property to make a profit, you must still report your rental income"; the question uses that test ("rented not to make a profit"). A filer with a bona fide profit objective is renting to make a profit even with losses, and p527 p. 24's presumption ("more than your rental expenses for at least 3 years out of a period of 5") is a presumption, not a requirement.

More than one exception on one distribution is asked by retirement.early_screen ('or more than one exception to the additional tax applies to it') and refused through retirement.screen_refused.

unruled:qbi.unreported_loss#1.reason: Suspended losses are asked by qbi.suspended and PTP losses are refused with every K-1; a loss left off a filed Form 8995 is a rare residual.

findings.evidence: i8995a p. 6, 'even if the loss was unreported': a loss left off a Form 8995 that was filed (for example for REIT dividends only) is neither in qbi.carryforward nor asked here. Rare; low.
qbi.suspended, asked with the same Schedule C gate: 'are you ... deducting a business loss or expense of an earlier year that a tax limit kept you from deducting then?' (refused; i8995 p. 3).
A PTP loss arises on a Schedule K-1, refused by scope.k1.
An unreported loss already absorbed before 2025 gives Yes and a refusal; extra refusing only.
K-1 losses are refused by scope.k1; a year with no return filed is a year 'whose tax return had no Form 8995'. Low.

unruled:sd.home_sale#1.reason: All three findings are WIDE (a Yes refuses where the gain is excludable); each is now named in the help.

findings.evidence: i1040sd p. 2, Reduced Exclusion: the help now says 'A smaller exclusion may apply after a move for work, health or other unforeseen reasons (see Pub. 523)'; a refusal costs coverage, not a value.
i1040sd p. 2, Sale of home by surviving spouse: the help now gives the $500,000 limit 'on a joint return or, not remarried, within 2 years of your spouse's death'.
i1040sd p. 2, Exceptions to Test 1: the help now says 'service abroad can extend the 5 years'.

unruled:gate:div.other_boxes_if_dividend.reason: The less-common-boxes question counts a share of a form in another's name.

findings.evidence: div.other_boxes help: 'Count your share of a form in another's name, and a payment with no form'.
Boxes 2b to 2d open the box 3, 9, 10 and 13 questions too; extra asking only.

unruled:gate:retirement.is_code2#1.reason: Code 7 series changes were not asked (BUG-1291, fixed); the change wording is wide by one-time switches.

findings.evidence: p590b p. 26. A series changed in 2025 with a code 7 payment is not asked; with code 1 it is asked by retirement.early_screen. Filed and fixed as BUG-1291 (medium): s2.other_tax names the recapture.
A one-time switch to the RMD method or a depleted account (p590b p. 26, 'not treated as a modification') answered Yes refuses a return with no recapture; extra refusing only.

unruled:gate:s1.uc_any#1.reason: Disability payments paid in place of unemployment compensation are a known low gap; the WIDE readings only open the amount question, which takes box 1 of a Form 1099-G.

findings.evidence: p525 p. 29, Types of unemployment compensation, 'Disability payments from a government program paid as a substitute for unemployment compensation'. Filed with the other state disability and medical leave benefits.
A Yes only opens s1.uc_paid, which asks the total of box 1 of each Form 1099-G; payments not reported there give no amount.
The same: a private fund pays no Form 1099-G box 1 amount (p525 p. 29 sends it to line 8z, refused elsewhere).
Medical leave benefits from the employee's own contributions are excluded (Rev. Rul. 2025-4 holding 4) and carry no Form 1099-G box 1 amount; the Yes only opens the amount question.

unruled:sb.trust_owner#1.reason: A transferor-owner under section 679 set up or funded the trust and is refused by sb.line8, asked first.

findings.evidence: i1040sb p. 3, Line 8, 'were you the grantor of, or transferor to, a foreign trust'. sb.line8 asks whether the filer set one up or at any time gave, sold or lent anything to one that still existed in 2025; a Yes refuses before sb.trust_owner is asked.

unruled:scope.f8978#1.reason: The question names only a partnership and an audit; i8978 also requires Form 8978 for a Form 8986 from an S corporation, trust or estate and from an AAR (new, low); the timing cases only widen.

findings.evidence: i8978 p. 2: 'Every partner (except pass-through partners) that receives a Form 8986 from a pass-through entity must file Form 8978', pass-through entities including 'S corporations, trusts ... and decedents' estates'. A current owner is refused by scope.k1, but a former S corporation shareholder or trust beneficiary answers No to 'a partnership that you ... were in'. New, low.

i8978 p. 1: Form 8978 reports Forms 8986 'because of a BBA examination or a BBA partnership AAR filing', with a separate 'AAR Filing' box. A partner whose Form 8986 comes from an AAR reads 'changes made by an audit' as No. Same new entry, low.

i8978 p. 2, reporting year 'includes the date the audited or AAR partnership furnished the Forms 8986'. An earlier-year Form 8986 answered Yes refuses a return whose line 6l and line 16 amounts are zero; coverage only.
A Form 8986 furnished in early 2026 belongs to the 2026 reporting year (i8978 p. 2); a Yes over-refuses and a No is correct, so no amount is wrong.
